title: Beef, steak, strip, lean and fat

content.title: About
content.content: Beef strip steak is a cut from the short loin of the cow. It can be lean or well‑marbled, which determines its flavor and juiciness. The steak is usually cooked on a grill, pan or oven, sliced 2–4 cm thick.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The strip is one of the most tender beef cuts because it has little connective tissue.
Marbling (intramuscular fat) enhances taste and keeps the steak moist.
Traditionally the steak is served medium‑rare to preserve tenderness and flavor.
In the US it is called “strip steak”, in the UK it is known as “sirloin steak”.
Beef is a rich source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant iron.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A strip steak provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Heme iron supports hemoglobin levels, while zinc is important for immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef contains B12, B6, niacin and riboflavin, which are vital for energy metabolism.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: The fatty portions supply monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that can support heart health when eaten in moderation.

items.title: Creatine and carnitine
items.content: These compounds help improve physical performance and aid fat metabolism.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake of fatty cuts may raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked beef can harbor pathogens such as E. coli.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: A marbled strip steak is calorie‑rich and can contribute to weight gain if over‑consumed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the steak hot, sliced against the grain. Season with salt, pepper and herbs, and pair with vegetables, potatoes or sauces such as béarnaise or mushroom sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, wrapped in plastic film. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C and use within 3–4 months.
